Each of these points on this space represents a small segment of a large sound file.

Using audio descriptors each segment is assigned two values from dimensionality reduction (UMAP) that attempt to represent the perceptual differences between this corpus.

The fluid.kdtree~ performs the function of mapping our mouse inside the space, to the point that has the most similar set of descriptor values. In effect, it is a fast lookup mechanism so that we can scrub through the analysis space.

Because the range of distances is hard to predict a priori, you can use the knearestdist message to get an idea of useful values for radius.
We can query the tree in terms of either a (maximum) number of neighbouring points to return, or a radius around the query point.
